summary: Thorough, well-researched analysis that correctly decomposes the issue #805 incident into three distinct root causes with precise, verified code references. The recommended combination approach (pre-phase branch reset + prompt guardrails + shell timeout + gateway branch enforcement) is sound and appropriately balances safety with implementation simplicity.
analysis: The analysis correctly identifies three cascading root causes from the issue #805 incident: (1) push rejections from branch history contamination across pipeline phases, (2) a runaway grep that searched the entire container filesystem for 22+ minutes, and (3) a completion signal accepted without verifying the agent pushed to the correct branch. All code references are verified accurate — I checked all 10 cited locations including _sync_worktree_with_remote() at orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py:1835-1934, get_changed_files_in_push() at gateway/git_client.py:1108-1210 with its three-tier diff strategy, the push denial hint at gateway/gateway.py:808-814, the 2-hour session timeout at sandbox/llm/claude/config.py:19-25, the completion signal handler at orchestrator/routes/signals.py:134-213, Pipeline.branch at orchestrator/models.py:270, auto_commit_worktree() at gateway/post_agent_commit.py:126-333, refine phase allowed patterns at gateway/phase_filter.py:490-496, branch-lock enforcement in the gateway, and the local-ahead skip behavior at lines 1892-1914. Every line number and behavioral description matches the actual code. The options analysis is well-structured: 4 options for push failures, 3 for runaway commands, 2 for completion validation — all meaningfully different with clearly articulated trade-offs. The recommendation of Option B (pre-phase reset) over Option A (scope-limited diff) is well-justified: it avoids modifying security-critical gateway diff logic while addressing the root cause. The combined E+F recommendation for runaway commands (soft + hard guardrails) is a sound defense-in-depth strategy. The 8 open questions are specific and actionable, covering implementation ambiguities that genuinely require human input (reset behavior for local-ahead state, timeout values, enforcement strictness, backward compatibility). The constraints section correctly identifies the single-branch-per-pipeline design as intentional and notes the tension between branch lock and push failure recovery.
suggestions: 1. The causal relationship between Root Cause 1 and Root Cause 2 deserves more attention. The analysis describes both failures but does not explicitly trace whether the push rejection triggered the runaway grep (i.e., did the agent search from '/' because it was trying to find the contract file after the push failed?). If so, fixing Root Cause 1 may significantly reduce the likelihood of Root Cause 2 recurring in similar situations, which affects prioritization. 2. The analysis notes the push denial hint message at gateway/gateway.py:808-814 is 'misleading in the pipeline context' but does not include improving the hint message in the recommendations. A clearer error message (e.g., 'This is a known issue with cross-phase branch history — the orchestrator should reset before your phase starts') would help agents respond appropriately even before the underlying fix is deployed. 3. Option F (Shell Command Timeout) mentions Claude Code's Bash tool supports per-call timeouts but does not investigate whether Claude Code supports system-wide default timeout configuration or hooks. This feasibility question would strengthen the recommendation — if Claude Code has no mechanism for enforcing default timeouts, Option F may require wrapping the shell itself rather than configuring the tool. 4. The analysis could note whether this is an isolated incident or a pattern across pipelines. If other pipelines have hit similar push failures without triggering runaway commands, that suggests Root Causes 1 and 3 are the higher-priority fixes.
